name: Simba Supermarket
location: Kigali (a Kigali Heights store and a Gahanga branch are named in BUY-01); 15 branches nationally
buys: Groceries including fresh produce and 'locally sourced products' (items not named); meat counter not confirmed
approach: Ask at a branch or head office for the local-supplier and category-buyer process; once the farm has stock, bring graded samples, a price list and packaging; ask payment days, rejection rules and delivery windows.
notes: Operating in 2026 (anniversary article, August 2026). Official site not located, so no contact copied. MD is named in the article but is not used as a contact. Local-sourcing claims are generic; no evidence yet that Simba buys fruit or meat directly from small farms. URL found by DNS probing; the page text was not readable to automated fetch (title 'Simba Supermarket - Better Quality, Better Life'), so official status is inferred and no contact is copied. A trade-press summary of a 2025-2026 broadcast quotes Simba's deputy manager saying not all needs, especially fresh produce, can be met locally and that local supply chains are developing (BUY-56): a hint of unmet demand for local fresh produce, or of quality and consistency gaps [assumption to test].

name: Sawa Citi (SPAR Rwanda licensee)
location: Kigali (first SPAR store in Nyarutarama, April 2025; Sawa Citi stores reported in Kimihurura, Remera and Kimironko in a 2021 guide)
buys: Groceries including fresh produce and frozen/meat (items not named); SPAR positions itself as 'premium yet local'
approach: Same as Simba. Premium positioning suggests tighter grade and packaging; ask for the SPAR Rwanda produce buyer and whether local fruit is sourced directly or through distributors.
notes: Operating since at least April 2025 (BUY-02). URL is the franchisor's country page; Sawa Citi's own site not located. The Amsterdam contact on that page is SPAR International's, not copied. Store count and 2021 locations are from BUY-25 (D) and are unconfirmed. Sawa Citi founded about 13 years ago and employs about 300 (BUY-56).

name: Afri-Farmers Market
location: Kigali (five outlets, newest in Kabeza, opened 2025-12-19)
buys: Fruit, vegetables, meat products and other farm goods bought from farmers; sells in stores, online with home delivery and to hotels, restaurants and schools
public_contact: Phone +250 732 422 466 (store at KG 2nd Street, Kimironko, per the company site)
approach: Strongest early-channel lead: ask how it onboards a new farmer (variety list, minimum volume, grading, collection days, price basis, payment); it collects from farms and pays immediately per a supplying farmer.
notes: Evidence for direct purchase: a supplying farmer quoted in BUY-03 says the company collects from the farm, weighs and pays immediately. Self-reported; no volumes, prices or specifications published. No website located, so no contact copied. Company site (BUY-44) confirms 2026 trading, lists categories fresh fruit, fresh meat and fresh vegetables, and has no supplier sign-up page. Its online price list (BUY-63) shows fruit at retail premium positioning and no goat or sheep item among the meat lines read.

name: GET IT
buys: Fresh produce distribution to hotels and restaurants (named as a local supplier by Heaven)
approach: Ask whether it takes new outgrowers or small lots, its produce list and grading, and whether it handles meat. Do not approach until its 2025-2026 status is confirmed.
notes: Named as a local supplier on Heaven's site (BUY-16). Third-party profiles (not opened in this pass) describe a hotel and airline fresh-produce distributor with an out-grower model; official website not located and 2025-2026 trading status not confirmed. Caution: the old domain getitafrica.com redirects to a domain-for-sale page (2026-10-19) and no 2024-2025 trading evidence was found; getit.africa resolves behind a Cloudflare block (HTTP 403 to automated fetch), so the company may still trade there, but the site could not be read and no URL is recorded until confirmed.

name: German Butchery
buys: Meat for its own retail and onsite restaurant and, per a 2021 guide, for many Kigali supermarkets; animal species and sourcing not published
approach: Ask which animals (cattle, goats, sheep) it buys, from whom, at what live or carcass spec, and which abattoir it uses.
notes: Named as a local supplier by Heaven (BUY-16) and as a supplier to supermarkets by a 2021 guide (BUY-25, D). Official site not located; status 2025-2026 not confirmed.

name: Kimironko Market
buys: Fruit, vegetables and meat sold by traders; July 2026 retail beef prices were reported from this market
approach: Visit on two weekday mornings with the price-collection sheet; identify 3-5 fruit wholesalers and one or two meat traders; ask who buys directly from farms and what they pay on delivery.
notes: Market operating in July 2026 (prices reported by BUY-09). Fruit and goat prices not captured in this pass. Market management contact not found.

name: Nyarugenge Market (Nyarugenge Modern Market)
buys: Fruit, vegetables and meat sold by traders; July 2026 retail beef prices were reported from this market
approach: As for Kimironko Market. Mid-2025 goat and sheep meat was Rwf7,500/kg at this market per a separate 2025 report (not opened in this pass).
notes: Operating in July 2026 (BUY-09). Market management contact not found.

name: Saban Abattoir (Saban Ltd), Nyabugogo
buys: Slaughter service for cattle, goats and sheep brought by traders; not a buyer of live animals
approach: Learn its slaughter fees, hours, inspection and ante-mortem rules, and how traders and butchers procure goats and sheep; use it to find the buyers of dressed goat. Do not treat it as a customer for live animals.
notes: Operating in July 2026 (BUY-09). RAB 2022 (BUY-10) says slaughterhouses give slaughter service only and return the meat to traders, and that Nyabugogo slaughtered at least 120 goats and 40 sheep a day. July 2026: four days without goats or sheep (BUY-09). Head of veterinary services is named in the article; not used as a contact.

approach: Ask for the Director of Food and Beverage or purchasing manager through the hotel switchboard; bring a product spec sheet and offer a tasting lot; ask about their approved-supplier process.
notes: Open per the July 2026 UN hotel list and a 2026 page footer (BUY-11, BUY-14). Phone from the hotel's page (BUY-14); email as published in the UNEP list (BUY-11) is a reservations mailbox, not a purchasing contact. Goat/mutton mention: BUY-10 Annex 1.
